rationale: Evidence from iteration 8, the best raced design at 683.09 (up from 633.93). Narrowing the sensor array to x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03 (sensor_size 0.016, kp 3.0, kd 0.8, ki 0, base_speed 1.0) gave these results. Oval held 20 of 20 finishes, with progress 0.997 and steering_oscillation falling from 0.30 to 0.13. S-bend finishes rose from 15 to 17 of 20. Slalom progress rose from 0.371 to 0.563, the largest slalom gain so far, though slalom still has 0 of 20 completions and 1.0 line-loss events per run. The Evaluator's keep-spacing rule applies: slalom progress is above 0.37, the oval is at 20 of 20, and s-bend finishes are at 14 or more. So I keep the narrower spacing and sensor_size 0.016. Spacing is therefore the slalom lever, and the Evaluator's next test is base_speed. Change (one variable from the best design, iteration 8): controller.base_speed 1.0 to 0.9. The slalom's alternating bends are the likely limit on its off-track exits, so a slower entry should give the sensors more time to track the line. Geometry, kp 3.0, kd 0.8, ki 0 and line_loss last_direction stay unchanged. Speed cost: the s-bend mean finish was 2.43 s at speed 1.0, so at 0.9 it should be about 2.7 s, which still clears the 3.0 s limit. The completion-time term loses only a little score, and that is far less than the value of converting slalom off-track ends into completions. Expected result, which is a hypothesis and not a measurement: slalom progress rises above 0.56 and slalom max_error falls below 0.06, while the oval stays at 20 of 20 and s-bend finishes stay at 14 or more. Risks: slower speed may raise the s-bend finish time close to the limit and cut its completions; a lower speed may also let the robot stall on the slalom if progress stops rising (the stall rule needs 0.002 progress per 50 steps). Reading the race: (a) if slalom progress or completions rise and the oval and s-bend hold, base_speed 0.9 is the better slalom setting, and the next step is a small sweep around 0.8 to 0.9 or a sensor spacing refinement to 0.025 steps; (b) if s-bend finishes fall below 14 or completion times approach 3.0 s, return base_speed to 1.0 and keep the iteration 8 design as the base; (c) if slalom stays flat near 0.56, bend geometry is the limit, and the next test should be kd or sensor spacing rather than speed. Measurements wanted: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and control_effort on all three tracks, so that speed effects on slalom can be separated from s-bend completion times.
